bull_bear.body:
- Integrated textile solutions positioning with an extensive portfolio of over 200 fabric-finish variants and advanced dyeing and printing capabilities serving large-scale, customised orders
- Jafrabad LNG terminal secured by 4.5 MMTPA binding regasification agreements with major public sector undertakings, described as giving long-term revenue visibility once commercial operations commence
- Shipyard infrastructure functional post-resurrection with an experienced engineering and execution team and strategic tie-ups with domestic and global players
- Order-backed, asset-light petroleum trading framework that minimises inventory price risk and preserves working capital
- Real estate land holdings and assets available for strategic development and monetisation
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical trade disruption and energy price volatility around the Strait of Hormuz — Regional conflicts and localised tensions disrupt standard maritime routes and global energy trade flows, inflating international pricing, raw material costs and freight rates for the oil and gas business.
- FSRU deployment dependency for the LNG terminal — Operational timelines remain tightly coupled with the successful conclusion of negotiations and finalisation of deployment contracts with global Floating Storage and Regasification Unit providers — the terminal cannot start commercial operations until this is resolved.
- Trading margin compression from supply-side disruption — Supply disruptions and procurement bottlenecks constrain localised trading margins and require highly agile inventory risk management to protect profitability.
- Shipbuilding execution and project delivery risk, with import dependence and raw-material price volatility — Large, technically complex mandates need stringent multi-phase scheduling and multi-vendor execution where delays hit profitability; deep reliance on foreign suppliers for critical maritime technology and propulsion systems adds currency and supply risk, while steel, specialty alloy and marine equipment price swings compress margins under fixed-price contracts.
- Competition from state-subsidised international shipyards — Yards in China, South Korea and Japan benefit from significant state subsidies, making it persistently hard for Indian shipbuilders to compete on pricing and delivery schedules.
- Coastal/climate exposure of operating facilities — Facilities located in coastal areas are inherently exposed to cyclones and heavy monsoons, which can adversely affect construction schedules.
- Textile cost competitiveness and subdued global absorption — Cost undercutting from low-wage economies, specifically Bangladesh and Vietnam, pressures pricing power and margins, while demand uncertainty in mature overseas export zones challenges export volumes and delays revenue realisation.
- Chemical management, effluent and regulatory compliance in textile finishing — BRSR material issues: finishing fabrics requires dyes, bleaches and softeners that are strictly regulated, where exceeding permissible limits can cause non-compliance, recalls, litigation, reputational damage and loss of market access; the water-intensive dyeing, bleaching and finishing processes generate effluent, emissions and hazardous waste, and the evolving compliance framework across environment, labour, chemical usage and product safety can bring penalties, operational disruption and restricted market access.
- Real estate input cost swings and cyclical absorption — Unpredictable steel, cement and labour wage costs threaten project-level profitability, while hyper-local competition across metropolitan submarkets demands calibrated launch velocities to sustain sales momentum and limit holding costs.
- Raw material sourcing concentration and supply chain transparency — Limited supply chain transparency and dependence on geographically dispersed sourcing networks expose the Company to material shortages, supply disruptions and price volatility, potentially causing delayed shipments and margin pressure.

business.body: On a standalone basis the Company is an integrated textile solutions provider offering over 200 fabric-finish variants ranging from 100% cotton to polyester-cotton, linen and viscose blends in lycra and non-lycra forms, backed by dyeing and printing capabilities, alongside construction of residential and non-residential buildings. Through its subsidiaries the group runs petroleum products trading, the Jafrabad FSRU-based LNG regasification terminal, shipbuilding and ship repair at Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Limited, and residential and commercial real estate development. Customers span eleven Indian states and one international market, with commercial and defence shipbuilding mandates from international owners and governments.

- **Shipbuilding:** 18,000 DWT IMO Type II chemical tankers, 92,500 DWT dual-fuel ammonia bulk carriers, Naval training vessel (defence export)

outlook.body:
- Scale shipbuilding and defence capabilities at Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Limited (SDHI) across commercial, defence and green shipbuilding
- Progress operationalisation of the Jafrabad LNG terminal — finalise FSRU chartering with global suppliers and agree phased ramp-up structures with offtakers
- Unlock value across the real estate portfolio through land bank development, asset monetisation and expansion of the Bengaluru residential pipeline
- Run petroleum trading on an order-backed, demand-driven model with lower inventory exposure and optimised working capital, with an expanded focus in the UAE
- Strategic restructuring of UAE exposure via the proposed sale and transfer of assets and liabilities of subsidiary Verasco FZE to de-risk capital investments
- Reduce debt and strengthen the capital structure, particularly in the real estate division
- Maintain operational discipline and cost efficiency in the textile business
- Strengthen execution capabilities and operational efficiencies across the diversified businesses as the Company moves into FY 2026-27
- The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy, published among its policies on the Company's website, mapped to NGRBC Principles P1 and P4. For the financial year 2025-26 the Board has recommended a dividend on the equity shares for members' approval at the 118th AGM, to be distributed out of the profits for the year ended 31st March 2026 and paid to members on the record date. Related-party remuneration to relatives of directors holding offices of profit is reviewed and recommended by the Audit Committee under the Company's Policy on Related Party Transactions and placed for members' approval under Section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013. The Company also maintains a Policy for Determining Material Subsidiaries.
- Adherence to globally recognised textile standards — OEKO-TEX Standard 100, GOTS, OCS and GRS — for dyes, bleaches and softeners, with emphasis on eco-friendly and certified chemicals
- Testing and quality assurance through NABL-accredited laboratories, with enforced safe storage, handling and disposal practices and employee training on chemicals
- Effluent management at the Ahmedabad unit through a multistage process — clarification, aeration, biological treatment and polishing via sand and carbon filters before discharge to CETP NTIEM; sludge dried, packed and disposed at a licensed TSDF facility
- Air-emission controls including ESP modifications, water scrubbers and Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS)
- Compliance management framework regularly updated to evolving laws, reinforced by board-level oversight, employee training, internal reviews, and external audits and certifications such as ISO and OEKO-TEX
- Occupational health and safety framework covering employees and on-site workers, with periodic safety training, welfare and healthcare initiatives and a formal grievance redressal mechanism; contractors are expected to meet the Company's health, safety and ethical standards
- Structured grievance redressal mechanisms for communities, investors, shareholders (SEBI SCORES), employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with no complaints pending resolution at the close of FY 2025-26
- Responsible sourcing — diversified supplier base, approved vendors meeting quality and compliance requirements, periodic supplier performance monitoring against environmental and social standards
- CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and is identified in the BRSR as an opportunity to enhance brand value
- Material responsible business conduct issues are benchmarked to the SASB 2023-24 standards; management reports no negative impact from the identified risks in the reporting period FY 2025-26
- Board-level Risk Management Committee frames, implements and monitors the Risk Management Policy, with the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risks and internal controls; internal financial controls were tested during the year with no material weaknesses observed
- Internal Committee constituted under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 with training and awareness programmes conducted through the year and no complaint received during the year
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Oil and Gas: the Jafrabad LNG terminal of Swan LNG Private Limited is in an advanced-stage pre-operational phase, with the jetty and associated marine facilities completed and breakwater works near completion; of an approximately `4,500 crore total committed project cost, over `3,500 crore has been invested in the terminal and associated infrastructure. The Company is working towards finalisation and deployment of the Floating Storage and Regasification Unit with leading global FSRU suppliers, and is engaging offtakers on commercially viable, phased ramp-up structures, with commercial operations planned to commence as market conditions normalise. Real Estate: Cardinal Energy and Infrastructure Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, is expanding its Bengaluru residential development pipeline and is developing "BODHI" at Jayanagar, Bengaluru — a premium project that secured Karnataka RERA approval and IGBC Gold Pre-Certification during the year, with construction advancing on schedule as the 6th floor slab was completed; the division also expanded its commercial footprint in Mumbai while maintaining IT and business parks in key tech hubs, and reduced total debt by ~12.5% from `129.41 crore to `113.20 crore as on 31st March, 2026. Shipbuilding: Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Limited scaled execution capability and revitalised its order book, securing a USD 227 million order from Rederiet Stenersen AS, Norway for six 18,000 DWT IMO Type II chemical tankers, an order for four 92,500 DWT dual-fuel ammonia bulk carriers from Energy ONE Limited, and a defence export mandate from the Government of the Sultanate of Oman for a Royal Navy of Oman training vessel; a 25% capital subsidy under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme is cited as enabling cost-effective brownfield expansion and infrastructure modernisation. Trading: a strategic restructuring is underway involving the proposed sale and transfer of assets and liabilities of subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, alongside a pivot to an order-backed, lower-inventory model. Standalone footprint per the BRSR is 1 plant and 1 office in India with no international locations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's structural shift toward a gas-based economy, expanding regasification capacity and City Gas Distribution networks underpins long-term demand for the LNG business
- Delays in major global liquefaction projects are expected to keep the LNG supply-demand balance relatively tight through 2026 and 2027, while Strait of Hormuz tensions drive spot LNG, crude, freight and marine insurance costs
- Global shipbuilding demand driven by fleet replacement cycles and IMO decarbonisation mandates compelling a transition to green, dual-fuel and LNG-powered vessels; the global market is projected to grow from USD 175.71 billion in 2026 to USD 274.19 billion by 2034 (Fortune Business Insights)
- Indian shipbuilding policy tailwind — a `69,725 crore shipbuilding and maritime reform package (September 2025), SBFAS 2.0 with a `24,736 crore allocation valid through 2036, Infrastructure Status for large ships lowering borrowing costs, and a 25% capital subsidy under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme
- Domestic vessel demand pipeline — an aggregated government requirement for 437 vessels estimated at `2.2 lakh crore, and a projected 80% expansion in the Indian Navy's frontline combat fleet by FY30
- Real estate premiumisation and urbanisation — rising white-collar incomes driving premium residential demand in hubs like Bengaluru and Hyderabad, with commercial leasing fuelled by Global Capability Centres and technology firms
- Textile sector supported by a domestic market projected to reach USD 350 billion by 2030, PM MITRA parks and the PLI scheme, and newly activated Free Trade Agreements, offset by soft global demand and cost undercutting from Bangladesh and Vietnam
- Company-level levers cited: continued scale-up at SDHI, advanced readiness of LNG infrastructure, real estate portfolio expansion alongside ongoing debt reduction, and stabilising textile and petroleum performance
- SDHI completely revitalised its commercial order book during the year and secured commercial & defence shipbuilding orders plus ship repair projects
- USD 227 million contract from Rederiet Stenersen AS, Norway, for six 18,000 DWT IMO Type II chemical tankers — described as one of India's largest commercial shipbuilding contracts and the first chemical tanker order awarded to an Indian shipyard; the agreement includes an option for six additional vessels
- Order for four 92,500 DWT dual-fuel ammonia bulk carriers from Energy ONE Limited, marking entry into the green vessel segment
- Defence export mandate from the Government of the Sultanate of Oman to construct a training vessel for the Royal Navy of Oman
- The shipyard delivered around twenty ship repair and refit projects during the year
- Jafrabad LNG terminal backed by contracted regasification capacities, with SLPL engaging offtakers on phased ramp-up structures

open.item: Stated FY 2026-27 priorities are scaling shipbuilding and defence capabilities, unlocking value across the real estate portfolio, progressing operationalisation of the LNG infrastructure, and strengthening core businesses.
The FSRU-based LNG infrastructure project has reached an advanced stage of readiness, with management planning commercial operations to commence as market conditions normalise.
Against a total committed project cost of approximately `4,500 crore for the Jafrabad LNG terminal, over `3,500 crore has been invested towards the terminal and associated infrastructure.
The Jafrabad LNG terminal is secured by 4.5 MMTPA binding regasification agreements with major public sector undertakings, expected to generate revenue once commercial operations commence.

Management expects the expansion of the real estate portfolio alongside ongoing debt reduction to drive sustainable future growth, with continued commitment to prudent capital allocation and strategic asset monetisation.
The Company initiated a strategic restructuring involving the proposed sale and transfer of assets and liabilities of its subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, to de-risk capital investments.
The Company is developing "BODHI" at Jayanagar, Bengaluru, a premium residential project targeted at upper mid-income and luxury buyers.
The Company will prioritise land bank development and asset monetisation across key markets to ensure debt reduction and value creation.
Swan LNG Private Limited remains focused on operationalisation of the Jafrabad LNG terminal, with the jetty and marine facilities complete and breakwater works near completion.
Of the approximately `4,500 crore total committed project cost for the Jafrabad LNG terminal, over `3,500 crore has been invested to date.
The USD 227 million Rederiet Stenersen AS contract for six 18,000 DWT IMO Type II chemical tankers includes an option for six additional vessels.
CEIPL is developing "BODHI" at Jayanagar, Bengaluru; the project secured Karnataka RERA approval and IGBC Gold Pre-Certification with construction on schedule at the 6th floor slab.
Strategic restructuring involving the proposed sale and transfer of assets and liabilities of subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, to de-risk capital investments.
The Jafrabad LNG terminal carries a total committed project cost of approximately `4,500 crore, of which over `3,500 crore has been invested.
The Company is working towards finalisation and deployment of the Floating Storage and Regasification Unit, with discussions underway with leading global FSRU suppliers.
